+//! Hidden alias names of renamed built-in posts (#3537, #4000). Provenance:
+//! CamCraft's own post registry history; no list shows an alias name.
+//!
+//! A saved project (document post, setup post, option key `builtin:<name>`),
+//! a script `cps:`, an MCP or CLI post name and a machine `controller.post`
+//! that still say an old name select the registry name. A save writes the
+//! registry name.
+
+use crate::schema::PostRef;
+
+/// `(old name, registry name)`, one row for each old name of a built-in post.
+pub const POST_ALIASES: &[(&str, &str)] = &[
+    // #3537 renamed it; #4000 renamed it again.
+    ("Agie native wire EDM", super::agie::POST),
+    // #4000: the name between #3537 and #4000.
+    ("Native wire EDM job files", super::agie::POST),
+];
+
+/// The registry name that `name` selects: the registry name for an alias, else `name`.
+#[must_use]
+pub fn current_name(name: &str) -> &str {
+    POST_ALIASES
+        .iter()
+        .find(|(old, _)| *old == name)
+        .map_or(name, |(_, new)| *new)
+}
+
+/// `post` with an alias name replaced by the registry name it selects.
+#[must_use]
+pub fn current_ref(post: PostRef) -> PostRef {
+    match post {
+        PostRef::Named(name) => PostRef::Named(current_name(&name).to_owned()),
+        other => other,
+    }
+}
+
+/// An option key `builtin:<alias>` rewritten to the key of the registry name.
+#[must_use]
+pub fn current_key(key: &str) -> String {
+    match key.strip_prefix("builtin:") {
+        Some(name) => format!("builtin:{}", current_name(name)),
+        None => key.to_owned(),
+    }
+}

+## #4000 - The AgieVision post is named "Agie Wire EDM (AgieVision)"
+
+**Decided.**
+- The post that writes AgieVision ISO, SBR and SBL job files for the
+  AGIECUT Classic 2S is named "Agie Wire EDM (AgieVision)". The name
+  follows the other wire posts: brand, process, control ("Sodick Wire EDM
+  (Mark 21)"). The contributor and the maintainer agreed the name on
+  Discord on 25 Nov 2026.
+- Its refusals say "The Agie Wire EDM job requires ...". The post dialog
+  says "AgieVision job files (ISO, SBR, SBL)" and "the AgieVision
+  control". The `.cps` option group is "AgieVision technology".
+- The two old names "Agie native wire EDM" (#3537) and "Native wire EDM
+  job files" stay hidden aliases. One table, `posting::aliases`
+  (`crates/app/src/posting_aliases.rs`), holds them. The project loader,
+  the option-key normalizer, `SelectPost`, `SetSetupPost`, `resolve_cps`
+  (scripts, MCP, CLI) and the machine `controller.post` check call it. No
+  generic module calls `posting::agie` to resolve a post name.
+- A save writes the new name. The project file version does not change.
+- The UI command `CommandKind::ImportAgieDrawing` is now
+  `ImportInspectionDrawing`: it runs a plain DXF import. It is internal to
+  the UI; no MCP tool, CLI command or script verb names it.
+- Kept: the condition ids, the MCP tool names, the CLI command, the
+  module names, the golden folder names, and the script receipt value
+  `"format": "Agie native wire EDM"` (scripts can read it).
+
+**Why.** #3537 removed the machine brand from the post name. The generic
+result "Native wire EDM job files" made a one-control post look like a
+feature of all wire machines. The control name in the post name tells the
+user which control the job is for. The name keeps "Wire EDM", because
+Agie also builds die-sinking machines.
+
+**Dropped.**
+- "AgieVision job files" (the audit's short form). Dropped: it does not
+  match the brand + process + control form of the other wire posts.
+- A neutral refusal in `crates/geometry/src/die_opening.rs` with the post
+  name added by the app caller. Dropped: the issue asks only for the
+  rename; the refusal now says "The Agie Wire EDM job requires ...".
+- Change the script receipt `format` value. Dropped: scripts read it, so
+  a change is a breaking change.
+- Post the legacy project in `wire_post_alias.rs` (the #4022 review asked
+  for a posting round-trip). Dropped: the control-checked punch fixture
+  and the job goldens live in the `agie_native` suite. The posting
+  round-trip is the submodule `agie_native/legacy_name.rs`, which reuses
+  that fixture. A copy of the fixture in a second test binary would
+  drift.
+- Keep the site anchor `#native-wire-edm-job-files`. Dropped: the one
+  link to it (`posting.md`) now points to the new heading anchor
+  `#agie-wire-edm-agievision`.
+
+**Cost to change.** Small: the name is `posting::agie::POST`; a later
+rename adds one row to `POST_ALIASES`.

In the machine editor, open **EDM** and add a condition with ID **AGIE_QN2**, role **rough**, wire diameter **0.25 mm** and preview gap **0.005 mm**. Apply this change to the mounted machine. Choose **Agie Wire EDM (AgieVision)** in the post picker.
 2. Define axis-aligned rectangular stock at most 350 × 250 mm in plan. Choose a stock thickness of 15, 20, 40 or 80 mm. The stock and work origin together must fit that span. Verify the installed work datum and the available axis travel on Agie Control. CamCraft refuses profiles with a stated X or Y travel limit because its preview cannot check the full resident path against that limit. Put the first, unrotated work origin on the stock top. Its XY position determines the job coordinates.
 3. Use one modeled workpiece and create one **Wire Contour**. For two to nine punches on the same stock, follow **Group captured punches** below. For a die opening, follow **Select a die opening** below. For two openings in one plate, follow **Group two die openings in one plate** below. For a punch, select the complete punch model. Use a punch with straight sides, vertical walls and flat ends at the stock planes. Angled faces are supported. Leave at least 0.4 mm of stock around the nominal polygon. Acute corners can need more stock: the post also checks the intersection of the two offset face lines and the swept wire at that corner. CamCraft checks each corner with the measured rough offset for the selected stock thickness. The stock margin includes the 0.125 mm wire radius. Some reentrant contours are supported. A tight inside corner fails if the rough offset for the selected stock thickness leaves more than 0.002 mm at the nominal vertex. Short segments and closely spaced faces fail if adjacent rough paths could meet. The punch must have a straight outer face that allows the lead to stay entirely on the waste side. Additional bodies, selected subprofiles, holes and steps are refused. Select a 0.25 mm wire and condition **AGIE_QN2**.
